text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.25% today, bouncing back from a two-week slide that had knocked the stock down 6.18%. The rebound comes as oil prices stabilized—US crude climbed back above $96 a barrel after falling on Thursday's report that Asian refiners are importing record volumes of oil, which had briefly suggested oversupply. The mixed signals from Middle East geopolitical tensions (Iran-US talks raising hopes one day, then criticism of appeasement efforts the next) have left oil traders uncertain, but the bounce in crude prices today provided enough lift for the stock to recover some ground.

The broader context is that energy stocks have been whipsawed by conflicting forces: geopolitical risk premiums from the Iran conflict pushing prices up, offset by signs that global oil demand may be softer than expected. ConocoPhillips' recovery today reflects traders reassessing the near-term supply-demand balance rather than any company-specific news.
